Lake District Circuits for Motorcyclists

The English Lake District packs extraordinary scenery into a compact area. Its lakes — Wordsworth's "beloved lakes" — are ringed by fell roads that provide some of England's most rewarding motorcycle riding. Here are the best lake circuits.

Ullswater Circuit

  • Distance: 22 miles
  • Route: Pooley Bridge → A592 (east shore) → Glenridding → A592 (Kirkstone direction) → minor roads back to Pooley Bridge
  • Highlights: The A592 along Ullswater's east shore is widely considered the most beautiful lake road in England. Aira Force waterfall is on the route. The view from Hallin Fell car park across the lake is stunning.

Derwentwater and Borrowdale

  • Distance: 15 miles (out and back from Keswick)
  • Route: Keswick → B5289 through Borrowdale → Honister Pass (optional extension)
  • Highlights: Ashness Bridge (the most photographed bridge in the Lakes), Castle Crag, the Bowder Stone, and the journey into the heart of Borrowdale — one of England's most beautiful valleys.

Windermere Circuit

  • Distance: 30 miles
  • Route: Ambleside → A591 (west shore via ferry) or → A592 → Newby Bridge → east shore → Ambleside
  • Highlights: The Windermere ferry crossing (a brief but charming car ferry), the west shore road through Claife Heights, and views of England's longest lake from multiple angles.

Thirlmere

The A591 runs along the east side of Thirlmere, but the narrow west shore road is the motorcyclist's choice. It winds through dark forest with glimpses of the reservoir between the trees and views up to Helvellyn.

Buttermere and Crummock Water

  • Distance: 10 miles (circuit of both lakes)
  • Route: B5289 circuit with Honister Pass on one side and Newlands Pass on the other
  • Highlights: Two stunning lakes connected by a short flat stretch. The Honister Pass approach from the Buttermere side is dramatic. Scale Force, England's tallest waterfall, is a walk from the road.
The Lake District's roads are narrow, popular, and often single-track. Summer weekends are busy with tourist traffic. For the best riding experience, visit midweek or in the shoulder season (April-May, September-October) when the roads are quieter and the light is dramatic.

Combining Lake Circuits

The Lake District is compact enough to link several lake circuits in a day. A suggested full-day route:

  • Start at Keswick → Derwentwater and Borrowdale
  • Over Honister Pass to Buttermere
  • Newlands Pass back to Keswick
  • A66 to Ullswater → circuit of Ullswater
  • Over Kirkstone Pass to Windermere
  • Circuit of Windermere back to Ambleside
  • Total: approximately 90 miles, 5-6 hours with stops

This route links three lake circuits with three mountain passes — a day of extraordinary variety in one of England's most beautiful corners. keyTakeaways: The A592 along Ullswater's east shore is widely considered England's most beautiful lake road.
The B5289 into Borrowdale passes Ashness Bridge, the most photographed bridge in the Lakes.
The Lake District is compact enough to link three lake circuits and three passes in a 90-mile day.
Many Lakeland roads are narrow, single-track, and busy, so ride midweek or in the shoulder season.
Aira Force waterfall and the Windermere car ferry add interest to the Ullswater and Windermere circuits.

faq.q: Which is the best single lake circuit for scenery?
faq.a: Ullswater is hard to beat. The A592 along its east shore is widely rated the most beautiful lake road in England, taking in Aira Force waterfall and the superb view from Hallin Fell car park. The 22-mile circuit is compact and can be extended over Kirkstone Pass towards Windermere, making it an ideal centrepiece for a Lakeland day.

faq.q: When should I ride to avoid the crowds?
faq.a: Midweek and in the shoulder season, roughly April to May and September to October, when the narrow roads are quieter and the light is at its most dramatic. Summer weekends bring heavy tourist traffic to single-track lanes and passes, turning great riding into slow queuing. Early starts also help you enjoy honeypots like Borrowdale before the day-trippers arrive.

faq.q: Can I combine several lake circuits in one day?
faq.a: Yes. A classic full day starts at Keswick, takes in Derwentwater and Borrowdale, crosses Honister Pass to Buttermere, returns over Newlands Pass, then heads via the A66 to circuit Ullswater before crossing Kirkstone to Windermere. That links three lake circuits with three mountain passes over roughly 90 miles and five to six hours with stops.

faq.q: What is the Windermere ferry like on a bike?
faq.a: The Windermere car ferry is a short, charming crossing that saves a long ride around the lake and adds a bit of novelty to the circuit. Ride on carefully, follow the crew's directions, and use first gear and gentle control on the ramps, which can be slick. It lets you link the quieter west shore road through Claife Heights into your route.
